observation.happening: Meeting notes interface displaying a completed Q4 migration planning meeting with structured decisions and action items, followed by a timestamped comment thread with speaker attribution.
observation.most_important: Hierarchical organization of meeting outcomes into Summary, Decisions (2), and Action Items (3) with clear reference numbering and subsequent chat/timeline view showing who said what and when.
observation.next_action: Expand sections, follow up on action items, play recording, or add comments to timeline.
anomalies: Clean structure with no visual inconsistencies
Right metadata (今日・42分・5人) clearly shows meeting duration and participant count

3361.why: Well-executed interface with clear information hierarchy, thoughtful section organization, and proper visual distinction between summaries, decisions, and action items. Layout is professional and functional, but the sidebar navigation and content arrangement follow standard patterns common in modern project management tools. Design is solid but not distinctively innovative.

observation.happening: Home/welcome screen for voice-first meeting notes application. Friendly greeting followed by primary action (what to finish), two recording options, schedule integration section, and getting-started tips with keyboard shortcuts.
observation.most_important: Voice-recording is core interaction (microphone icon in input). Greeting creates welcoming tone. Generous whitespace throughout. Onboarding section educated new users without overwhelming. Calendar integration mentioned but gated behind permission.
observation.next_action: Start recording, enable calendar access, use Space key to begin, or review tips.
anomalies: Large empty space in center is intentional breathing room
References 'previous settings' suggesting returning user experience
Calendar permission gate is clearly explained

398B.why: Exceptionally well-designed empty state with masterful use of whitespace and hierarchy. Greeting establishes friendly tone. Onboarding section shows genuine care for new users. Geometry is balanced and inviting. However, centered content with guidance text is a common pattern in modern apps. While execution is excellent, the underlying layout pattern is not distinctive enough for SUPREME.

observation.happening: Minimal header or toolbar component showing Notion as selected context. Includes Notion icon and dropdown indicator. Dark gray background.
observation.most_important: Acts as a selector or navigation element indicating current tool context.
anomalies: Image is very small and shows only a single component
No context for what this component is part of larger

4001.why: This is an isolated header or toolbar component showing only the Notion selector. Without seeing the full context, surrounding interface, interactions, or how this component fits into the larger design system, meaningful evaluation of design quality is impossible. The component itself is adequately proportioned but tells us nothing about the overall design.

observation.happening: Success notification/toast message indicating completion of weekly briefing creation. Shows action name, context (created from 2 sources), and action buttons (Open, Copy, Close). Green success indicator on left.
observation.most_important: Clear success state with immediate next actions. Provides context about what was created and source count. Button layout allows user to proceed or capture output.
observation.next_action: Open briefing, copy content, or dismiss notification.

4870.why: Well-executed success notification with clear state indication, appropriate button layout, and calm dark background. The green success indicator and contextual information (source count) demonstrate thoughtful design. However, this follows standard notification patterns found in most modern applications. Execution is polished but the pattern itself is not distinctive.
